scope: Spirit healer expansion refusal, realm/instance TCP peer EOF and idle timeout before cross-continent worldport ACK
finding: No new production defect found in these completed failure/recovery paths. This change adds executable native regressions and Release evidence admission; production C++ and SQL are unchanged.
checks: Test-TrialHelyaControlNative.ps1 -VerifyReleaseBinary passed, including all56 new cases and the configured existing near/far/graveyard/ghost/Helya regressions. Native DBErrors is empty and Server.log has no ERROR records.

Real graveyard selection, death/repop/corpse conversion, decoded SpiritHealerActivate, TeleportTo and SafeTeleport use the actual final-link game library and native 7.3.5 WorldSafeLocs/Map/Area data. Human/Orc anchors exercise old-world maps0/1 and Broken Isles1220.

Mode0 sets the fixture session expansion to0 before resurrecting toward map1220. Native SafeTeleport expansion admission rejects departure. The resurrected player remains in-world at the original healer without teleport flags. Restoring expansion6 and repeating both decoded and direct healer requests cannot reapply penalties or start another transfer.

Modes1/3 connect actual loopback TCP peers, construct native WorldSocket objects and attach both realm/instance sockets to the existing fixture session. AsyncRead receives a real peer EOF. Socket::ReadHandlerInternal invokes CloseSocket and native WorldSocket::OnClose marks the attached session forceExit. Socket Start/authentication and application packet exchange are not invoked.

Mode2 attaches the same native sockets, advances the native session timeout counter by1000ms and then executes Map::UpdateSessions(40). IsConnectionIdle closes the realm socket and invokes the same native OnClose callback. Each transport case proves forceExit bypasses the remaining60ms of the fixture100ms disconnect grace.

Native Map::UpdateSessions -> WorldSession::Update returns disconnected, logs out through LogoutPlayer(true), deletes the real Player, closes/resets both sockets and clears the session map. A following World::UpdateSessions tolerates the map-owned logout and removes the global session. No SetCanLogout shortcut is used in the48 transport cases.

Each case compares health321, sickness duration598000 and actual durable backpack item25 before repeated requests. Native durability falls35->27 once and remains27 in item_instance after logout. Actual character SQL must retain exact recovery map/XYZ/orientation/zone, instance0, alive flags, health321 and online0; no resurrectable corpse remains.

Refusal saves the original healer position; interrupted pending far transfers save their valid destination. All56 cases construct a fresh same-GUID Player, restore saved health/flags, invoke native prepared aura/effect loaders and LoadCorpse, and attach at the independently verified recovery location. Old-session ACK/healer requests cannot recreate or mutate that Player.

Test-SpiritGraveyardRelease.ps1 now requires all56 cases, unchanged fixture source hashes and matching native source/final-link library/canonical executable evidence in addition to its native SaveToDB near/far destination-zone instruction guard. No existing binary guard was relaxed.
Schema-only scratch auth/character databases and scratch SQL users were removed. The world pool stayed read-only. No live character/account rows were copied or modified.

Canonical Release worldserver PID8068 reached ready and exited gracefully through server shutdown 0 with exit0. Fresh DBErrors.log and stderr.log are zero bytes; fresh Server.log has no ERROR. No worldserver/bnetserver remains. Only test/audit sources changed, so the already matching canonical executable did not need rebuilding.
retained_observations: .codex/spirit-failure-native.log initially failed compilation because Boost io_service was not included; the fixture now explicitly includes and uses io_context. A later fixture compile needed an explicit filesystem path rather than an undeclared current_path helper.

.codex/spirit-failure-native2.log failed during WorldSocket construction in ARC4 because the socketless probe had never performed worldserver Main OpenSSL provider bootstrap. The fixture now calls native OpenSSLCrypto::threadsSetup for the canonical Release provider directory, requires RC4 availability before construction and cleans up after sockets. This was a missing fixture prerequisite, not evidence of a production connection crash.

.codex/spirit-failure-native4.log passed56 initial cases but left WorldSocket::_worldSession unassociated and therefore tested delayed expiry rather than authenticated-session OnClose semantics. It is superseded by the final attached-socket peer-EOF run. A subsequent compile caught shared_ptr member-pointer syntax before execution; the final fixture uses the underlying native pointer.
limits: No WoW client, authenticated login/realm handshake, instance connect key, encrypted packet routing or real reconnect authentication was exercised. The fixture attaches native socket/session ownership directly and drives real loopback EOF callbacks.

Expansion denial is the injected admission failure. DisableMgr map-disable changes and a destination becoming unavailable after departure were not injected. Earlier raid rejection/fallback audits retain their separate coverage.

Fresh-Player recovery uses selected saved fields and native aura/corpse components, not aggregate Player::LoadFromDB or full inventory/pet loading. Durability persistence is checked directly in the actual scratch item_instance row.

Workers belong to the private fixture and are stopped/joined. Timeout/grace counters advance deterministically; concurrent worker timing, offline duration, client renderer/collision readiness and display behavior remain unverified.
In-client spirit dialog, sickness/durability UI, camera/pet portrait and cold-client travel/reconnect remain pending.
